summary.oneLiner: Strong Q4FY26 performance driven by 22% revenue growth and 30% EBITDA margin, fueled by new product launches (Dalbavancin, Multivitamin) and CDMO expansion, with full-year EBITDA margin rising to 26% and Cenexi turning EBITDA-positive; what matters is the sustained margin expansion from high-value products and Cenexi’s path to mid-teens EBITDA, positioning Gland as a global complex injectables leader.
summary.business: Gland Pharma develops, manufactures and markets complex sterile injectables and generic injectable formulations, together with APIs, and provides contract development and manufacturing (CDMO) services to global pharmaceutical companies. Its portfolio spans liquid vials, lyophilised vials, pre-filled syringes, ampoules, infusion bags, ophthalmic products and cartridge-based delivery, serving oncology, ophthalmology, Central Nervous System (CNS) disorders and hospital critical-care segments. The company operates primarily on a business-to-business model with a specific focus on complex injectables, NCE-1s, First-to-File products and 505(b)(2) filings, and the 2023 acquisition of Cenexi localised manufacturing and development capability within Europe.

currentContext.strengths: 45+ years of experience in sterile injectables manufacturing, with operations in high-barrier regulated markets (U.S., Europe, Canada, Australia, New Zealand)|Regulatory track record across multiple sites - USFDA approvals at Dundigal, Visakhapatnam SEZ and Pashamylaram, and EU approval for the Visakhapatnam SEZ oncology plant|Breadth of sterile delivery formats (liquid and lyophilised vials, pre-filled syringes, ampoules, infusion bags, ophthalmics, cartridges) allowing deployment across multiple critical-care therapy areas|European manufacturing and development footprint acquired through Cenexi, described as making Gland an end-to-end, multi-geography partner to global pharmaceutical leaders|In-house R&D infrastructure since 2000 at Dundigal, supporting complex injectable technologies, NCE-1s, First-to-File products and 505(b)(2) filings|Scale: 11 manufacturing facilities across finished formulations and APIs and ~1,700 Mn units/year of sterile injectable capacity (including Cenexi)|4,300+ employees as of March 31, 2026 supporting the base business
currentContext.strategies: Expand the CDMO business and position Gland Pharma as the strategic partner of choice for global pharmaceutical companies seeking scalable injectable solutions, by integrating development expertise with manufacturing strength.|Deepen specialisation in complex injectables - peptides, long-acting injectables, suspensions and hormonal therapies - as the source of competitive advantage and deeper market penetration.|Build an expanding footprint in advanced drug delivery systems, specifically pens and cartridges, including the partnered GLP-1 platform.|Continue expanding across both regulated and emerging markets to strengthen global presence and secure resilient revenue streams.|Sustain targeted investment in R&D, complex injectables, drug-device combinations and co-development partnerships (R&D expenditure was ~5% of base business revenue in FY 2025-26) to build a differentiated pipeline.|Pursue a differentiated pipeline spanning NCE generics, first-to-file opportunities and 505(b)(2) pathways.|Leverage sterile injectable capability across 15+ therapeutic areas and 7 dosage forms as targeted diversification to strengthen market relevance in high-value segments.|The Company states it is committed to driving superior value creation for all stakeholders, with the focus continuing to be future growth and the long-term interests of the Company and its shareholders; accordingly the Board 'would continue to adopt a progressive dividend policy, ensuring the immediate as well as long term needs of the business'. The Dividend Distribution Policy, framed under SEBI LODR and annexed to the Board's Report, lays down the criteria the Board considers before recommending a dividend, including ensuring the Company has sufficient distributable profits and/or general reserves as determined from a review of its audited financial statements prior to any declaration, and defines the form and time periods within which dividends are paid. Talent retention is supported through two Employee Stock Option Schemes (ESOP Scheme 2019 and ESOP Scheme 2025), administered by the ESOP Compensation Committee, with no changes made during the year. During the year the Company did not extend any loans or guarantees or make any investments covered under Section 186 of the Companies Act, 2013, other than an investment in its wholly owned subsidiary. There is no disclosed buyback, debt-reduction target or credit-rating commitment in the supplied text. The Company has no Associates or Joint Ventures during FY 2025-26.|Occupational health and safety management system aligned with the ISO 45001 standard, supported by a Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment procedure (SOP GSE024) and a Near Miss / Incident Reporting System (SOP GSE013).|National and international standards adopted and mapped to the NGRBC principles: ISO 45001:2018, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 9001:2015 and WHO GMP certificates.|Replaced furnace oil with piped natural gas (PNG) as boiler fuel at all manufacturing facilities, stated to have significantly reduced stack emissions and lowered CO2 output.|Bio-medical waste and wastewater management: effluent and sewage treatment plants at manufacturing facilities are regularly screened and upgraded, with strategies implemented for the treatment and recycling of wastewater.|Water stewardship: significant improvements to the raw water underground storage tank and continual enhancement of the water quality sampling process, stated to have reduced overall water consumption.|Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) applies and the waste collection plan is in line with the EPR plan submitted to Pollution Control Boards; packing waste goes to approved scrap vendors, e-waste to authorised recyclers and hazardous waste to State Pollution Control Board-approved TSDFs.|FY 2025-26 disclosed environmental and safety outcomes (Key Highlights): 15.77% of energy derived from renewable sources, a 69.50% reduction in High Speed Diesel (HSD) oil consumption for steam generation, 2,969.85 MT of waste utilised and zero fatalities across manufacturing facilities.|BRSR disclosures carry a Reasonable Level of Assurance from DNV Business Assurance India Private Limited.
currentContext.expansion: Expansion in FY 2025-26 is framed around two of the company's six strategic priorities - augmenting manufacturing capacities and capabilities, and the foray into complex CDMO including biologics. On capacity, the Company states it is commissioning additional manufacturing lines to support future growth across complex injectables and sophisticated delivery formats, scaling capacity through greenfield investments, and commissioning new production lines at the Pashamylaram facility for suspensions. Cartridge fill-and-finish capacity is being expanded to 140 million units per year; the GLP-1 platform note describes this as pen and cartridge capacity 'being scaled from ~40 million to 140 million units per year to meet anticipated demand growth', while the MD&A future-growth section states the Company has 'already expanded our cartridge fill-finish capabilities, from the present 40 Mn to 140 Mn' - the report is not internally consistent on whether the expansion is complete. The Company also states it is ramping up ophthalmic suspension capabilities and investing in technologies to extend CDMO capability across new modalities including biologics, drug substance and specialised formulations. In biologics CDMO, the Company entered a long-term strategic collaboration with Dr. Reddy's Laboratories at its biologics facility in Genome Valley, Hyderabad, collaborated with Shanghai Henlius Biotech to manufacture select biosimilar products, is expanding drug substance capabilities across monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and other biosimilars, and has secured CDMO contracts for complex products across suspensions, hormones, emulsions, peptides and microspheres plus eight GLP-1 programme contracts. Cenexi's Drug Product capabilities are being leveraged to offer integrated solutions alongside Gland manufacturing. Geographically, expansion is targeted at emerging markets across Africa, the Middle East, Latin America, APAC and Rest of the World, with recent forays into Saudi Arabia, China, South Africa, Mexico, Taiwan and South Korea. On the environmental side of capital spending, 2.15% of FY2026 capex went into technologies improving environmental and social impact - an effluent (Cyto/Non-Cyto) collection facility modified at Unit II and the VSEZ facilities - against 0.35% and 3.65% in FY2025 (effluent storage tank capacity enhancement, secondary containment pits, effluent segregation, a new RO plant, and solar rooftop project installations). No commissioning dates or completion timelines are given for any of the manufacturing projects.

risks.note: Changes in regulatory requirements and compliance frameworks could impact operations and product approvals. The BRSR material-issues table also flags Regulatory Compliance as a risk with negative financial implications, noting the business 'can be influenced by frequent and intricate regulatory changes'. Mitigation is stated as strong regulatory compliance programmes and quality assurance systems aligned with global regulatory standards, plus active monitoring of amendments to rules, regulations and laws.

The pharmaceutical industry is described as highly competitive, with pricing pressure, product innovation cycles and new market entrants intensifying competition. The MD&A separately lists pricing pressures in generic markets and increasing competition among the conditions that may continue to influence operating performance. Mitigation is a focus on differentiated products and complex injectables plus sustained R&D investment and partnerships with global pharmaceutical companies.

Disruptions in raw material sourcing, logistics challenges or geopolitical developments may impact product availability and delivery timelines; the MD&A also cites fluctuations in raw material and energy costs. Mitigation is supplier-base diversification, stronger procurement monitoring and strategic inventory buffers.

Financial performance may be affected by market volatility, pricing pressures and operational inefficiencies; the MD&A additionally cites foreign exchange volatility. Mitigation is a diversified product portfolio, a strong balance sheet, strategic cost management and operational efficiency initiatives.

Cybersecurity threats, data breaches and IT disruptions could impact operational continuity and data integrity. Mitigation is leading-edge cybersecurity systems, robust IT governance, regular vulnerability assessments and employee awareness programmes.

Attracting and retaining skilled professionals remains critical for sustaining operational excellence and innovation. Permanent-employee turnover was 14% in FY 2026 (14% in FY 2025 and 23% in FY 2024). Mitigation is talent development initiatives, leadership programmes and employee engagement frameworks.

risks.risk: Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) / occupational health and safety risk
risks.note: Operational hazards may affect employee safety and environmental performance. The BRSR material-issues table classifies Occupational health and safety as a risk with negative financial implications. Mitigation includes an occupational health and safety management system aligned with ISO 45001, a Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment procedure (SOP GSE024) and a Near Miss / Incident Reporting System (SOP GSE013), plus safety training and environmental management practices.

risks.risk: Revenue concentration - single activity and heavy export dependence
risks.note: The BRSR reports 100% of turnover from a single business activity (pharmaceutical research and development, manufacturing and marketing of complex injectables) and exports at 88.44% of total turnover, making the business structurally exposed to a single therapeutic-technology platform and to overseas regulatory, pricing and geopolitical conditions - in particular the U.S., which management identifies as the key momentum market. This concentration is disclosed in the BRSR but is not itself labelled as a risk by the Company.

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.
